comments.text: SR's first instruction, the address the intro jumps to after loading SR: a jump to the start-up at $0DE7

Start-up and main loop. Resets the stack, runs sr_setup ($14CB, which loads and runs INIT), then loops for ever: each pass calls the per-frame routines in order, from the clock and flight update at $1239 to the screen update at $8ED3. $A470 returning carry set sends the loop back to its top early

The main loop proper: $1239 clock and flight update, $1BB2, $3689, $7634, $74D3, $787B, $75FC, $135F (keys), $6AB3, then $A470; if that returns carry set the pass ends here, otherwise $6519, $7772, $A488, $24B3, $798F and $8ED3 follow

Sets up the machine for play: the processor port's low bits to 01 (RAM with the I/O in), $02 to $40, a raster interrupt at line $32, CIA 1 interrupts off, and the vectors: NMI ($0318 and $FFFA) to $0E9E, BRK ($0316) and reset ($FFFC) to $0E9F, both an RTI; IRQ at $FFFE to $0EA0 and the KERNAL's $0314 to $0EA5, so the interrupt runs whether the KERNAL is banked in or not. Then clears the key buffer ($0ECD) and the sound ($1067), banks everything out ($0E85) and enables interrupts
Clears the low two bits of the processor port $01: all RAM, the I/O and both ROMs banked out. Called after every stretch of code that needed the chips or the KERNAL
Sets the processor port's low bits to 01: RAM everywhere except the I/O area at $D000-$DFFF
Sets the processor port's low bits to 10: the KERNAL ROM and the I/O in, BASIC out. Used around every KERNAL call the loader makes
The NMI handler: returns at once, so RESTORE does nothing
What the reset vector at $FFFC points to while the game runs: an RTI
The raster interrupt as entered through $FFFE (all RAM): saves A, X and Y, then falls into irq_body

The raster interrupt's body, also the KERNAL's $0314 target while the KERNAL is in for a load: saves the processor port and banks the I/O in; on a raster interrupt it acknowledges it, counts the frame in $16 (stopping at 255), reads the keyboard into the buffer ($0ED6) and steps the sound effects ($10D2), then restores the port and the registers
Empties the keyboard buffer: no keys waiting ($03 = 0) and room for two ($04 = 2)
Called by the interrupt every frame: scans the keyboard ($0EF5) and, when it returns a key, appends it to the buffer at $05; with the buffer full the oldest key is dropped to make room

Scans the keyboard, the C128's extra keys included: notes the CTRL ($13), left SHIFT ($14) and right SHIFT ($15) states, then reads the eight C64 rows and the C128's three extra rows through $D02F, ignoring the modifier keys (mask table $0FDC). Returns zero with no key, or a repeat not yet due (first repeat after 30 frames, then every 6). Otherwise returns the key's character from the table at $0FEF: CTRL with a letter gives its control code, SHIFT with a letter gives the capital, SHIFT with a digit or punctuation key gives the symbol from $1047/$1057. A key on the C128 keypad (index $40 or more) ignores the modifiers. Also clears $0D03 on any key
One byte per keyboard row, ORed into the row's read so the modifier keys never count as a keypress: row 1 bit 7 (left SHIFT), row 6 bit 4 (right SHIFT), row 7 bit 2 (CTRL)
The index of each row's first key in key_chars: 0, 8, 16, ... 80, eight keys a row for the C64's eight rows and the C128's three

The character each key gives, 88 entries in matrix order (row then column), ASCII with lower-case letters; $80 marks a key that gives nothing (the modifiers, RUN/STOP, C=). Entries from $102F are the C128's extra keys: the keypad digits and Enter, the cursor keys, ESC, TAB, LINE FEED and HELP
The unshifted keys that have a shifted symbol: 1-9, colon, semicolon, comma, full stop, slash, cursor down and cursor right codes
What SHIFT turns each key in shift_from into: ! " # $ % & ' ( ) [ ] < > ?, cursor up ($0B) and cursor left ($08)

Silences the sound: clears the three voices' effect timers ($28-$2A) and repeat counts ($2B-$2D), sets the voice mask $1D to $FF and the engine-hum flag $1E to 0, zeroes the three voices' frequencies and the filter routing, and sets the volume to full

Starts sound effect A (0-13; anything higher is ignored). The effect's tables at $11AD-$122B give its voice and its start frequency, frequency step, attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform, length, gate-off point and repeat count; they are copied into that voice's slots with interrupts off, and its timer cleared so the interrupt starts it on the next frame

Called by the interrupt every frame for each of the three voices: starts a waiting repeat of the voice's effect (resets the frequency, retriggers the envelope with the effect's waveform), otherwise adds the frequency step to the voice's frequency, takes the gate off at the gate-off point and silences the voice when its timer runs out. With voice 1 idle it plays the engine hum: a pulse whose pitch follows the speed in $0415 (its size, either direction), unless $1D or $1E masks it off
The SID register offset of each voice: 0, 7, 14
Per voice: the high byte of the frequency an effect starts at
Per voice: the low byte of the frequency step added every frame
Per voice: the high byte of the frequency step
Per voice: the current frequency, low byte
Per voice: the current frequency, high byte
Per voice: the effect's attack/decay value
Per voice: the effect's sustain/release value
Sound effect table, 14 entries: the voice each effect plays on (0-2)
Sound effect table: the frequency each effect starts at (high byte)
Sound effect table: the frequency step's low byte
Sound effect table: the frequency step's high byte ($FF for a falling sweep)
Sound effect table: attack/decay
Sound effect table: sustain/release
Sound effect table: the waveform and gate written to the control register ($81 noise, $41 pulse, $21 sawtooth, $11 triangle)
Sound effect table: how many frames each repeat lasts
Sound effect table: the frame count at which the gate is released
Sound effect table: how many times the effect plays

The main loop's first call. Counts down $0836; fires the beam ($20EC) when auto fire ($0CFF) is on, the player's target ($0445) is a ship slot (0-5) and $0D00 has counted down to zero; every seventh pass with $3A clear runs $3102. Every 256th pass: $1DDF, then the clock line ($923E with $044B), then, with fewer than three ships in slots 1-5 (in use, $0403 clear), it may add one: $2C8A picks a type from $077C divided by 8 (none if negative), skipped when $A2C5 is negative with two ships already present; $1D4A/$1D6A when $08F9 for that type is clear, then $1E73 and $1949 create it, and ships whose distance ($7947) is $0B49 or more are removed ($1A5F with A=$FF). Every 16th pass: counts $0D29 down to clear the message line ($A178), counts $0D00 down, and computes $0C04/$0C05 from $073B/$073C and a value from $2EDB and $B451
Counts main-loop passes down from 7 to the next flight step at $3102
Counts the 256-pass periods of frame_update

Calls $2419, then takes a key from the buffer ($A24D, letters as capitals) and runs its command: the key is looked up in key_cmds ($145C), only its first 25 entries (up to V) while $0838 is set; the handler's address less one is pushed from key_handlers ($1481) and reached with RTS. A key that is no command is dropped
Key A, 4 or cursor left: one step more turn to the left (the player's turn rate $0516 down, at most $46 either way)
Key D, 6 or cursor right: one step more turn to the right ($0516 up)
Key W, 8 or cursor up: one step more pitch ($0508 up)
Key X, 2 or cursor down: one step more pitch the other way ($0508 down)
Key S or 5: stops all rotation, pitch ($0508), turn ($0516) and roll ($050F) to zero
Key Z or 1: one step more roll ($050F down)
Key C or 3: one step more roll the other way ($050F up)
Key J: jettison. Calls $2ECF and prints the message at $CFCE
Key minus: unless $0D02 is set, one step less speed for the player's ship ($0415, slot 0 of the speed array), clamped to -$46; sets $0D01 to 1
Key plus: unless $0D02 is set, one step more speed ($0415), clamped to $46; sets $0D01 to $FF
CTRL-E (and the C128's HELP key): toggles $0D02, which the speed keys and $2419 test: cruise or Newtonian flight
CTRL-T or I: toggles $7C and redraws the TAC display ($311E, $3114)
Key L: toggles automatic beam fire ($0CFF), only when $073E (fitted equipment) is set
Key V: the next camera view ($0D3C counts 2, 1, 0 and wraps to 2), then redraws the view ($65B0)
ESC: waits for a key ($A431) with the engine hum off ($1E)
Key N: Navigation Control ($2543), with the engine hum off while it runs
Clamps X, a signed rate or speed, to -$46..$46

The 37 keys that are commands in flight, in the order of key_handlers: A 4 cursor-left, D 6 cursor-right, W 8 cursor-up, X 2 cursor-down, 5 S, 1 Z, 3 C, J, minus, plus, ESC, CTRL-E, HELP, V, T, CTRL-T, I, L, 0, space, R, full stop, N, CTRL-S, G, Return

The command handlers for key_cmds, each address less one (do_key reaches them with RTS): turn, pitch, stop, roll, jettison ($13D4), speed ($13DE, $13F3), ESC ($1438), flight mode ($1408), view ($142B), next target ($1D82), TAC mode ($1411), auto fire ($141D), fire ($1DBE), next weapon ($1E5C), navigation ($1442), save ($154E), surrender ($392A), and Return, which also takes the next target ($1D82)
High bytes of key_handlers' words: do_key reads each handler as the pair at $1481+2n
Run once from sr_init: sets up the interrupt and vectors ($0E22), swaps the KERNAL's zero page in ($17B5), loads INIT to $E900 and jumps to it; INIT's RTS returns to the main loop
Loads END to $E900 with the engine hum off: END is INIT's bytes, put back after a base has used $E900
Loads SEG0, the flight overlay, to $A500
Loads SEG1, the base overlay, to $A500 and SEG1A to $E400
Called after a save or an INIT reload: selects screen 0 ($1BEE), redraws ($8F40) and puts the view back ($9E4C with Y=0)

The ending: with the engine hum off, sets the disk prompt to BOOT ($1859), loads WON from side 1 to $6800, swaps the KERNAL's zero page back ($17B5) and jumps to WON at $6800. Reached from the docking routine when the base is the Manchi homeworld

CTRL-S: asks the question at $CF9B (Save game? Y/N, a key through $A24D). Y: $B981 and $8EF6, then the prompt is set to BOOT, SPB is loaded to $4000 as a check that the BOOT disk is in, and the game state $0403-$0801 is saved as "@0:SAVED" ($1783); the prompt goes back to DATA and the screen is restored ($1525). Any other key just clears the message line ($A178)

Sets up the objects of the sector the ship is in (from $7256 and INIT). $040F = $40; empties object slots 19-1 ($1A8A) and sets the 21-byte type list at $C6 to $FF; $1D4A; picks a list from sector_object_lists by the value $2F75 gives for the sector at $071E/$071F (divided by 8) and writes its object types into the type list from the top; then reads the sector's own entries ($3030 gives the pointer and count) through the system map's tables at $5590/$5550/$55B0, adding up to three objects of type below $64 (bit 7 at $5550 also copies three bytes from $5620 to $0778, $16B2) and counting entries of $64 and up in $0782; then creates every listed object ($167F and $1949), clearing $0445,y for one whose $060D matches $0D04 when $0D07 is set. Ends with the player's speed at 5 ($0415) and $0545-$054D cleared
Counts a system map entry of type $64 or more in $0782
Sets up position words for a new object: takes the object type's word at $0A1D, multiplied by 8, as the range in $60/$61, and calls $1E73 with the source block at $065D and destination $006B
For a map entry with bit 7 set at $5550: copies three bytes for it from the map's table at $5620 (indexed through $55B0) into $0778-$077A
Ten pointers to zero-terminated lists of (count, object type) pairs that enter_sector writes into the slots, chosen by the sector's kind
The high bytes of sector_object_lists' pointers, read in pairs with $16C9
The lists themselves, as (count, type) pairs ending with a zero count
One byte per sector kind (0-9, the kind times 16 from $2F75): bit 7 doubles the HELM travel time through it
Pointers per sector kind to the text QUERY gives for it (texts in the disk text at $CFxx; $1721 is an empty string)
The high bytes of sector_kind_texts' pointers
enter_sector's loop counter over the 21 slots
From INIT: puts object type 0, the player's ship, in slot 0 ($196F with X=Y=0, $74/$75 at $0DC3), sets $0433 (slot 0) to 4, then falls into copy_ship_stats

Copies six bytes of the player's ship ($0735-$073A) into the type-0 entries of the per-type tables ($0AA9, $0AAA, $0C2B, $0C45, $0C52, $0C6C), and $072A plus 2 into $0C79, so the player's ship is described like any other type

Loads a file through the KERNAL: X/Y point to its zero-terminated name, $80/$81 give the destination. Swaps the KERNAL's zero page in and banks the KERNAL in ($17C6), LOAD with secondary address 0 (to the destination), then puts everything back ($17F8); a failed load shows the disk prompt and tries again until it succeeds
Saves memory through the KERNAL: X/Y point to the name, $80/$81 the start and $82/$83 the end (exclusive). Same set-up and retry as load_file
Swaps $90-$C4 with the copy at $0190-$01C4: the KERNAL's own zero page goes in for a load, the game's comes back after. Called in pairs
Common start of a load or save: stops the engine hum ($1D = 0), keeps the name pointer, measures the name, swaps the KERNAL's zero page in, banks the KERNAL in, and calls SETLFS 1,8,0 and SETNAM
The operand of LDA # before SETNAM: the name's length, written by open_for_io
The operand of LDX # before SETNAM: the name's low byte, written by open_for_io
The operand of LDY # before SETNAM in open_for_io: the name's high byte, written by open_for_io

Common end of a load or save: banks everything out, swaps the game's zero page back, turns the hum mask back on ($1D = $FF); if the KERNAL returned an error (carry set) it shows the disk prompt ($1812). Returns with the KERNAL's carry and X/Y as they were
After a failed load or save: plays effect 4, prints "Insert " and the disk named by $1857/$1858 ("BOOT disk..." or "DATA disk..."), waits for a key and clears the line
The load address, then the save end address, kept for the retry
io_addr's high byte
The save's end address, low then high, kept by save_file for the retry
The save end address's high byte
The disk prompt's strings: "Insert ", "BOOT disk...", "DATA disk..."
Points to the disk name disk_prompt shows: $183D (BOOT) or $184A (DATA)
disk_name_ptr's high byte
Sets the disk prompt to "BOOT disk..."
Sets the disk prompt to "DATA disk..."

Reads one 256-byte block of the disk, by number, into ($80): A is the block number's low byte and Y its high byte. Converts it to a track and sector with the sectors-per-track table ($190A), writes them into the command "U1 5 0 tt ss", opens "#" as channel 5 and the command channel 15 with that command, and reads 256 bytes; on an error it shows the disk prompt and tries again
The RTS at the end of read_block, and the byte before the sectors-per-track table, which read_block indexes from track 1
Sectors on each track of a 1541 disk: 21 on tracks 1-17, 19 on 18-24, 18 on 25-30, 17 on 31-35
The channel name "#" and the block-read command "U1 5 0 tt ss" that read_block fills in
The track number's tens digit in read_block's command string
The track's units digit in read_block's command (the tens at $1935)
The sector number's two digits in read_block's command string
The sector number's units digit in read_block's command
read_block's count of bytes read
Converts A (0-99) to two ASCII digits: tens in X, units in A

Creates an object of type X in a free slot and returns the slot in Y ($FF if none was free). Types below $0D (ships and missiles) take a ship slot 5-1, types $0D-$10 slot 6 alone, types $11 and up a slot 19-7. Falls into fill_slot
Puts an object of type X into slot Y without looking for a free one (INIT uses it for the player's ship in slot 0)

Sets up slot Y for type X: marks it in use ($05F9, $0649), stores the type ($060D), sets $0635 nonzero when the type's $0A1D word is nonzero, takes the type's $0AA9 word as the slot's hit points ($051D), and copies the 9-byte position at ($74) into the slot's entry of the position block at $065D (9 bytes a slot, offsets from $0846; $9570). Slots 0-6 get their rotation rates cleared and the 27-byte record at $0DA8 copied into their entry of the block at $044B (27 bytes a slot, offsets from $083C; $90F6). Ship slots 0-5 get speed, $0409, $041B and $0403 cleared, $0445, $0439, $043F and $0433 set to $FF, and the 9-byte record at $0DC3 copied into their entry of the block at $0545. A ship in slots 1-5 whose type has flag bit 5 counts $0403 up; any other gets a random turn rate, $041B = 1, $043F = 0, $0433 from its type's $0C1E, and the three bytes $85-$87 that $3E0D returns stored at $0421+3*slot. Finally loads the type's model ($1C95)
Every path of fill_slot ends here: load the model for the type, and return the slot in Y, or $FF when the model could not be placed (carry set)
No free slot: return $FF in Y

Takes the object in slot Y out of play; A says how: $FF removes it quietly, 0 means the player destroyed it. Clears the TAC when it was the player's target ($311E), empties the slot ($1A8A); for A = 0 and a ship slot whose $0403 is clear, gives the reward ($1ABF); unless A is $FF, ends at $24F6 with the slot

Empties slot Y: clears its in-use flags ($0649, $0635, $05F9) and, among ship slots 0-5, every target ($0445) and $0439 that pointed at it, remembering in $8C the last ship that had it as its target. Slot 0 is the player's ship: freeing it is the end of the game ($1B90)

The player has destroyed the ship in slot $8A. A type-6 ship counts in $079A when $079C is set; then, by the ship's $0433: 0 adds a random amount and 3 adds nothing extra, and either adds 32 times its type's $0C79 to the credits ($2F22) with the messages at $1B96 and $1BAF; then, on a negative random number, takes the type's $0C79 off $072B, and when that borrows and $072A is below 5, puts $072B back to 7 shifted left $072A times and raises $072A ($1737 copies it). With a random number below $40 the standing ($3C90) changes: up with the faction of the ship that had targeted it ($8C), down with its own unless it is type $0C. A ship whose $0433 is 1 or 2 adds ($0C79+2)*16 to $0726/$0727
Slot 0 was freed: the player's ship is gone. Loads END (INIT's bytes) to $E900 and jumps into it at $E972

The main loop's second call. For every slot in use whose type has flag bit 3 (missiles, the type $22 object) its hit points ($051D) count down by one each pass; when they run out the object is removed ($1A8A), and if its $0403 was set it becomes a type $22 object in its place ($7C52, $1949)
Loads picture A (0 PIT.PAC, the cockpit; 1 NAV.PAC; 2 LAND.PAC; 3 H.PAC; names from the table at $1C15) to $4000 and unpacks it to the bitmap at $C000 (unpack_picture)
Pointers to the four picture files' names in the loader's name table: PIT.PAC, NAV.PAC, LAND.PAC, H.PAC
The high bytes of picture_names' pointers

Unpacks a picture from ($74) to ($78). First clears the 1 KB at ($78)+$2000 (the screen matrix that follows the bitmap) and sets the border black. The packed stream is a run of records: a byte n of 1-$7F repeats the next byte n times; $80+n copies the next n bytes; 0 ends it, and the byte after it is the border colour
Sets the border colour to A, banking the I/O in for the write

Loads the model for object type Y if the type has one ($093E) and it is not loaded yet. The file name is the model's 4-byte entry at $0961; it goes to the model heap's next free address ($1D80). Then relocates it there: the prologue's LDA #lo / LDA #hi (bytes 1 and 5) get the load address added, its stores and jump are rewritten to STA $7A, STA $7B, JMP $7C61 (the model drawer), and the 15 words from byte $11 get the load address added. Every type that uses the same model is pointed at it ($08F8/$08F9), and the heap pointer moves on by the size word at byte $2F. Returns carry clear
Forgets every loaded model: clears the model pointer of each object type that has a model, and puts the heap pointer back to $E400
Loads the model for every object in slots 19-1 ($1C95), after reset_models or a reload
The address where the next model will be loaded, $E400 after reset_models
model_heap_next's high byte

Key T or Return: auto fire off, then the player's target ($0445) moves to the next slot in use after it: a ship slot (1-5) with $0403 clear, slot 20's type, or an object whose type has flag bit 0 (bases, planets and the like) or is type $14; past slot 19 the target becomes none ($FF). Redraws the TAC ($311E, $3114)
Key space or 0: fires the selected weapon ($0CFE): 0 the beam ($20EC), 1-3 a missile of type 9, 10 or 11 ($1EAD), all from slot 0

Every 256 main-loop passes (frame_update): when the player's target is a ship slot whose $0433 is not 3, checks whether it targets the player in turn ($0445 of that ship, $387E) and, unless $0833 already says so, prints the message at $1E5B with the ship's name ($366D) and one of the texts from $CE9E chosen by its type ($0C) or $0433 and two random numbers; $0833 is set so it is said once
An empty string: target_status prints it to clear the message line before its own text
Key R or full stop: selects the next weapon downwards ($0CFE 3, 2, 1, 0 and round), skipping a missile type the ship has none of ($0731), then redraws ($3102)

Puts at ($78) the 9-byte position at ($74) moved by a random amount on each axis: the top two bytes of each coordinate (offsets 7, 4 and 1) get a random value from -R to R-1 added, where R is the word $60/$61 ($A27D gives a random number below 2R)

Ship slot Y launches a missile of type X (9, 10 or 11). Not when its $0409 bit 0 is set. A computer ship needs no ship with $0403 set and a nonzero $0433 present; the player needs $0836 at zero and one of the type left ($0732 + type - 10). The missile is created ($7C52, create_object); for the player it plays effect 7, uses up one missile and sets $0836 to $7E. The missile's $0433 is the launcher, its speed $4B; unless it is type 11 or the launcher has no target, it takes the launcher's target, $041B = 3, and $043F = 4 when a random number below 100 is under the target type's $0C2B (and the target is a ship without $0409 bit 5), else 2. It copies the launcher's $0545 block and 27-byte $044B block; a type 11 missile from a computer ship also gets $7C52/$92CC/$923E aiming work; its position comes from the launcher's ($9108, $934B, $9759)
The 9-byte vector launch_missile adds ($9108, with the launcher's orientation) to put a new missile ahead of its launcher: three 3-byte coordinates
Advances the clock by A hours: each time the hours ($0720) pass 23 they go back to 0 and the date moves on a day ($203A)

Moves the date on a day: counts days elapsed ($0724/$0725), then the day of the month ($0721) up to the month's length ($20AF), the month ($0722) up to 12 and the year ($0723) up to 99, each going back to 1 (the year to 0)
Prints the date: the day ($9F56), a space, the month's three letters (from $20B8) and the year
Prints the time: the hours ($0720, $9F56) and ":00 HRS"
":00 HRS", printed after the hours
The length of each month, indexed by month 1-12 (the byte before January is the string's end): 31 28 31 30 31 30 31 31 30 31 30 31
The months' names, four bytes each with a zero, JAN to DEC: print_date finds month m at $20B8 + 4m

Ship slot Y fires its beam, if its $0409 bit 1 is clear and its type has a beam ($0C52, kept in $A9). The player's beam goes along the ship's own axis (the vector at $045D); a computer ship's goes toward its target, the direction worked out into $0896 ($7C52, $92CC, $9669); no target, no shot. trace_beam finds what it hits. For the player a miss still draws the beam ($2279) with effect 12; a hit on the target (or on any ship slot for a computer ship, unless the victim's type has no $0AEF value or the shooter is its own $0433) does the damage ($2222). Each shot of the player's adds one to the beam heat $0D00, up to 8

Follows the beam from ship slot $A8 in 50 steps along the direction at $0896 (scaled by $95A0 and $934B from the word $0300 with $FF): at each step every object with a hit radius ($0635) other than the shooter is tested ($74A3) against its type's radius ($0A1D) plus 2. Returns the first slot hit, or $FF

The beam from slot $B2 hits slot $B3 with power $B4: draws it ($2279); effect 12 when the player fired; effect 1 and $0835 = $FF when the player is hit, effect 0 when one computer ship hits another. The damage is the table entry at $2414 for the power's low three bits, halved once for each step of the player's beam heat ($0D00); power 4 hits with X = $FF, the others with 1. Ends in $6EA0 with the shooter in X and the victim in Y

Draws a beam shot from slot $B2 at slot $B3 with power $B4, its pattern from $2410 ($8F80). From the player in the cockpit view ($0D3C = 0) it fills the two triangles of the cockpit's guns ($23F9 and $2405) between screen updates ($8EEB); from the player with nothing hit in another view, $901D. Otherwise it projects both ends ($23BA), skipping the shot when either is behind the viewer, and fills a thin triangle ($8288 with 3 corners at $FD00): the near end, the far end, and the far end moved 4 pixels along the shorter axis
Projects the point ($58) relative to ($5A) for the beam: subtracts ($92CC), rotates into the view ($9160 into $0896) and projects ($6773); returns $089E's sign (negative when the point is in front)

The two triangles draw_beam fills for the player's beam in the cockpit view, three corners of two words (x, y) each: (-2,0) (113,45) (23,0) from the top left, and at $2405 (252,0) (137,45) (227,0) from the top right, meeting near the view's centre
The right-hand gun's triangle for cockpit_beam_shapes: (252,0) (137,45) (227,0)
The fill value draw_beam passes to $8F80 for each power value 0-3
The damage of a beam hit for each power value 0-3

Called by do_key before the keys: reads the joystick. Fire fires the selected weapon. Up and down change the player's speed ($0415) by one, held at $46 and -$45, and refuse to cross zero in one push (a push from zero needs $0D01 clear); in Newtonian flight ($0D02) neither changes the speed. The direction pushed is kept in $0D01 (1, $FF or 0). Then, while $0D03 is set (no key pressed since the stick was used), the stick's smoothed position ($A3B1) sets the pitch ($0508) and turn ($0516) rates directly through joy_rates
The fire and speed part of joystick_flight: returns X = $FF after a push forward, 1 after a pull back, 0 otherwise
Sets the pitch and turn rates from the stick's smoothed X and Y ($A3B1), each divided by 8 and looked up in joy_rates, while $0D03 is set
Rotation rate for each sixteenth of the stick's smoothed travel: -10 -6 -4 -3 -2 -1 0 0 0 1 2 3 4 6 10 10

The main loop's call for the sector's hazards. While the sector has hazard entries ($0782), now and then (a random number up to $8B coming out $80 or more) it draws a flash of pattern 5 at a random place in the view ($8B24) with a random size from 1 to $C0; one of size $AD or more also plays effect 11 and strikes the ship ($6E8D)
Scatters debris where the object in slot Y was: up to ten objects of type $18 created at its position, each with a random velocity ($251E)
Gives slot Y a random velocity: each of its three 3-byte components in the velocity block at $0545 gets a random low byte and a top word of 0 or $FFFF by a second random number's sign
explode's count of debris objects still to make

Key N, Navigation Control. Prints "Switching to navigation panel", clears the view, loads NAV.PAC as the picture and NAV.TIL to $4000, draws the system chart ($2E7A, $8810, $2880), copies the ship's sector ($071E/$071F) to the chart's cursor ($C6/$C7) and to $5510/$5530, counts in $0D07 the ship slots whose ship has no target, then loops: date, time, the chart ($2669) and the menu ($25CA)

The Navigation Control menu: CHART, HELM, STATUS, QUERY, SCAN, COCKPIT (strings from $26F1; HELM is offered only when no ship is near, $0D07, and the chart's destination is set, $FC00 positive). The choice jumps to CHART $2787, HELM $2728, STATUS $2694, QUERY $2A69, SCAN $2619 or COCKPIT $2634
SCAN: moves the chart cursor with the keys ($27D6, $A33F, $264D) and redraws, until a key ends it

COCKPIT: when the ship has moved ($C8), takes the new sector from $5510/$5530 and sets it up (enter_sector); then leaves navigation by dropping the menu's return address and going back to the cockpit ($2E71)
Moves the chart cursor ($C6, $C7) by X across and Y down, unless that leaves the 32 by 32 chart
Redraws the chart around the cursor: marks the cursor's sector ($3069 with 5, $2F9C), draws ($8638, $28DD, $8658), and moves the frame counter $5E on every other call

STATUS: the status page is in the base overlay, so this forgets the models, loads SEG1 over SEG0, runs its status page ($AB87 with X = $1D, Y = $AE, A = 7), then loads SEG0 back and reloads the models
Loads NAV.TIL, the navigation chart's tiles, to $4000
Colours the HELM line of the menu: $5C, or $78 when X is nonzero, written to 7 cells of two screen rows at $E1FD and $E225
"Switching to navigation panel"
Pointers to the six menu items' names
The menu items' names: CHART, HELM, STATUS, QUERY, SCAN, COCKPIT
One flag a menu item: 1 offered, 0 greyed out (HELM's, at $2723, is set by nav_menu)
HELM's enabled flag in nav_item_enabled, written by nav_menu

HELM, the autopilot: flies the course in $FC00/$FC20 a sector at a time from the ship's chart position ($5510/$5530). When the course runs out it prints "Ship has arrived at destination" ($2847) and returns. Each step: draws the move ($30D7), marks that the ship moved ($C8), moves the ship's position, lets the time pass ($290F), recomputes the rest of the course ($2880), and stops when an encounter or a key ends it; recolours the menu when ships are near ($0D07)

CHART: the cursor starts on the ship; the cursor keys move it ($A33F, move_cursor) and each move makes it the destination ($072C/$072D) and recomputes the course ($2880). Return or Escape leaves; with a course set it prints "Course laid in Nav computer" ($282B). $072C = $FF (no destination) while the chart is open

Prints "SC" and the cursor's sector coordinates on the chart's info line ($9F56), and below it "-message-" when the sector at the cursor is one of the 31 entries of the system map's list at $5510/$5530 whose message word at $55D1 is not $FF, or blanks otherwise
"Course laid in Nav computer", then "Ship has arrived at destination" at $2847, "SC" at $2867, "-message-" at $286C and a blank line at $2876

Works out the course from the ship's sector ($5510/$5530) to the destination ($072C/$072D) as a list of sectors: each step moves one sector across and one down toward the destination, diagonal first; the X list goes to $FC00 and the Y list to $FC20, ended by $FF. No destination, no course
Marks each sector of the course on the chart: for each one visible ($3013) it plots ($8763) and changes the chart cell at $FA00 from $7D to 7

The time one HELM step takes: $29CA gives the hours (5 straight, 7 diagonal, doubled in slow sectors and with a damaged drive); the clock advances an hour at a time with the date and time redrawn, and a key ends the trip ($AB). When the day changes: damage repairs itself ($2A53), the daily lists $07AE-$07BB and $0783 are cleared and the random generator reseeded ($A2DC). Then the chances of the step: $2A15, $2D38, the view cleared, the encounter counters $0832-$0834 cleared and $2991. Returns $AB, nonzero to stop

Checks for an encounter in the step's sector ($2C1E with the hours); when one comes, prints "Under attack" (with ships near, $0D07) or "Space craft detected", plays effect 4 and waits 20 frames or a key, setting $AB to stop the autopilot. Sets $0D04 to $FF first

The hours a HELM step costs: 5 for a straight step, 7 for a diagonal one (A nonzero); doubled when the sector's kind ($2F75, divided by 16) has bit 7 in sector_kind_flags, and doubled again when the player's $0409 has bit 2 (a damaged drive)
"Under attack", then "Space craft detected" at $2A00
Per HELM step: a chance, A/2 in 100, quadrupled when the sector has a type-$64 map entry, that the first entry of the list at $0767 ($0777 entries) whose $0D08 is negative becomes $14
When $0740 is set, a new day clears random bits of the player's damage flags ($0409 ANDed with two random numbers ORed together)

QUERY: describes the sector under the chart cursor in the text buffer at $FA00 ($9DEE appends): the system's name from the map ($5505) and the coordinates, then "FEATURES " with a name for each of the sector's map entries that is a real object ($2BC0), and the sector kind's text (sector_kind_texts, a disk text when its high byte is $C0-$CF); then "SHIPS " with, for the ship's own sector, the objects it met there ($0D04-$0D06 after a HELM trip) or the ships present in slots 1-5 whose type's $0AEF is zero; "none" where a list is empty. Prints the buffer ($9AFA), then the first entry of the sector with a message ($55D0/$55D1 not $FF), and waits for a key
Ends a QUERY list: after names it takes off the last ", "; with none it appends "none"
Appends the name of map entry type A: types below $64 by the object type's name pointer ($0B12/$0B13), $64 and up from query_hazard_names ($2C12); then ", "
"none", then "FEATURES " ($2BF6), "SHIPS " ($2C00), two carriage returns ($2C07), ", " ($2C0A) and the line breaks at $2C0D
Two carriage returns, the separator after each QUERY section
Name pointers for map entry types from $64: type $64 is "Ion Storm" ($2C14)
The high byte of query_hazard_names' pointer for type $64

Rolls for an encounter after A hours of HELM travel: the chance grows with the hours and the system's danger level ($077C, both through $B451, less $495, $B5E0), kept in $96. Up to three ship types are drawn ($2C8C) into $0D04-$0D06 with their factions in $97-$99 (none: $FF); with at least one, $2CD2 decides whether they attack ($0D07). Returns the first type, negative for none
Sets the chance in $96, then picks a ship type as pick_ship does

A random number below 100 at or over the chance $96 gives no ship ($FF). Otherwise a second random number below 100 is spent across the system's five class weights ($077D-$0781) to choose a class, and a random number below 16 picks one of the class's four entries in ship_class_types ($2D24): mostly the first two, the third and fourth only when a random number below the player's rank value ($0C79, halved) reaches 4. Returns the type in A and its faction ($0C1E) in X

Decides whether the encounter attacks: if the second or third ship is hostile to the first ($387E returns $FE) they fight each other and leave the player alone; with $073D set, a random number below $56 also lets them pass; otherwise the first ship's attitude to the player ($387E with X=4): hostile ($FE) means an attack ($0D07 counts up), $FF or a neutral faction 0 attacks half the time (a negative random number)
Four object types for each of the five ship classes pick_ship chooses from: class 0 types 12 12 12 12, then 2 2 5 5, 7 8 7 8, 3 3 6 6, 1 1 4 4
Once a day of HELM travel: every map entry with a motion kind (flags at $5550, bits 0-2) is moved by its kind's routine, the address from map_motion_routines written into the JSR at $2D56
JSR whose operand move_map_objects rewrites to the entry's motion routine
Low byte of the JSR operand move_map_objects rewrites
High byte of the JSR operand move_map_objects rewrites
When a system map is loaded: puts each entry of motion kind 3 or 4 (the orbits) at its place for the date, through the JSR at $2D82 rewritten the same way
JSR rewritten by place_orbiting_objects to the orbit routine
Low byte of the JSR operand place_orbiting_objects rewrites
High byte of the JSR operand place_orbiting_objects rewrites
Motion kind 1: the entry moves a random step of -1, 0 or 1 across and down, staying on the 32 by 32 chart
Motion kind 2: an RTS, the entry stays where it is

Motion kind 3: places the entry on the 16-step orbit at $2E11 by the day count ($0724/2 plus the system's phase $5610). An entry whose picture ($5570) is $6C-$6F gets the picture for its quarter of the orbit ($2DD2)
Motion kind 4: places the entry on the 32-step orbit at $2E31 by the day count ($0724/4 plus $5611), then sets its picture like motion_small_orbit
The BPL that ends motion_large_orbit; its two bytes are also where motion kind 0 would read its routine in map_motion_routines
The BPL's offset byte, also the high byte motion kind 0 would read
The motion routine of each kind from 1: $2D89 wander, $2DB9 none, $2DBA small orbit, $2DEB large orbit
The 16 chart positions (x, y) of the small orbit, a circle of radius 3 around the centre of the chart (16,16)
The y coordinates of orbit_small's positions, read in pairs with the x at $2E11
The 32 chart positions (x, y) of the large orbit, a circle of radius 6 around the centre
The y coordinates of orbit_large's positions, read in pairs with the x at $2E31
Leaves navigation or a base screen for the cockpit: restores the picture and view ($1525), $A14C, and redraws the cockpit ($3102)

Loads the system map of system $071D: the file "Q" with the system's digit ($2EA0) to $5100. Copies the system's six encounter bytes ($5612: danger level and five class weights) to $077C-$0781 and places the orbiting objects ($2D60)
The system map's file name, "Q" and a digit load_system_map writes
The system digit of str_system_file, written by load_system_map
Puts cargo of kind A, amount X, into the first empty hold slot ($0767 negative; amounts in $076F). Carry set when the hold is full
Called from the base overlay (SEG1, $AF57): finds the first hold slot from the top holding cargo kind A ($0767 counted from slot $0777) and empties it ($FF); returns with Z set when none was found
Empties every hold slot ($0767-$076E set to $FF, $0777 slots)
Counts the hold slots in use: returns 0 for none, $FF for a full hold, otherwise the count
Prints the disk text $CF9C+A
Takes the word $60/$61 off the credits ($0728/$0729) if there are enough: carry set when paid, clear (and nothing taken) when not
Adds the word $60/$61 to the credits ($0728/$0729), stopping at $FFFF
Clears the view window, x 24-199 and y 40-183 ($8E17), and draws it in pattern 1 ($8F80, $901D)

The kind of the sector at X, Y on the loaded system map: the tile code in the 32 by 32 grid at $5100 (row 31-Y; the LDY's operand at $2F96 is rewritten), looked up in the tile set's table at $5000. The kind is a multiple of 16
LDY from the map grid; sector_kind writes the address of row 31-Y into its operand, and X picks the column
Low byte of sector_kind's rewritten LDY operand
High byte of sector_kind's rewritten LDY operand: the grid row's page

Puts the system map's entries into the chart window buffer at $FA00 around the cursor X, Y: each entry with a picture ($5570, a tile code) inside the window ($3013) replaces the cell ($8763 finds it) unless the cell's tile hides things (bit 3 of its attribute at $5000). An entry with a heading (flag bits 3-4, set by set_ship_heading) shows the tile for that heading, a quarter or half the heading value added as the tile's attribute bits 0-1 allow; a tile with attribute bit 2 animates by the frame counter's low bits unless the entry's flag bit 5 is set
Carry clear when the sector X, Y lies in the chart window around ($51, $53): under 6 columns and 5 rows away. Returns X and Y as offsets from the centre
Lists the system map entries (of the 32 at $5510/$5530) that lie in sector X, Y: their numbers go to $3061, the pointer to the list in $74/$75 and the count in Y
The entry numbers sector_entries finds, up to eight

Fills the chart window buffer ($FA00, 11 cells across by 9 down, filled from the end) with the map grid's tiles around X, Y: columns X-5 to X+5 and rows Y-4 to Y+4 (rows counted from the bottom). Cells off the chart get tile A, or, when A is $2C, the tiles $2C and $2D in a checkerboard
The operand of CPY #: fill_chart_window writes $20 here for rows on the chart and 0 for rows off it, so a row off the chart takes the off-chart tile at every column
The operand of CPY #: fill_chart_window writes the window's left column here (X-6), where each row stops
Sets the heading of map entry A from the step X, Y: right 0, up 8, left $10, down $18, written into bits 3-4 of its flags ($5550); no step, no change

Redraws the cockpit's instruments (from frame_update every seventh pass, and after keys that change them): $8810, the speed ($31B2), the hit points ($3240), the weapon ($329C), the attack lamp ($3129) and the threat lamps ($314D), then falls into draw_tac
Redraws the TAC display: the data page ($336F) when $7C is 0, the target's picture ($3501) otherwise
Clears the TAC display: pattern 1 ($8F80), then $B788 and $B839 in SEG0
Lights the lamp at screen cell $E2F1 (and its copy at $62F1) in colour $8A when a ship in slots 1-5 whose type's $0AEF is zero has the player (slot 0) as its target; $C5 otherwise

Sets the three lamps at $E33B, $E363 and $E38B (with copies at $63xx): for each of up to three ships in slots 1-5 whose type's $0AEF is zero, a level of 1 for present, 2 with a target, 3 with the player as its target; each level picks a colour from threat_colours ($319F)
Colour for a threat lamp level X+1, 0-3, from threat_colours
The threat lamps' colours for levels 0-3: $BC $C5 $24 $8A

The speed readout. In Newtonian flight ($0D02) the shown speed is the ship's actual speed ($7C21, at most 99), also written to $0415; "CF" or "NF" (from $323A) is printed, a reversed mark when the drive is damaged ($0409 bit 2), then the number ($9F56); then the speed bar: $7C21's value (at most $42) fills the bar at x $18-$5A, row $21, in pattern 5 against pattern 1 ($8C23)
"CF" for cruise flight and "NF" for Newtonian, the speed readout's labels
The hit-points bar: the player's hit points ($051D/$051E) halved, plus one, at most $3C, drawn at x $4E, row $13, in pattern 4 against pattern 1, in pattern 7 (the warning colour) when under 15

The weapon readout at column $1E, row $1E. For the beam: a reversed mark when it is damaged ($0409 bit 1), the heat level ($0D00/2, at most 3) as one of four symbols, A or M for automatic or manual fire, then "-]". For a missile: its symbol ($7C), a reversed mark if the launcher is damaged, the count left, and a "*" in place of "]" when it cannot fire (damaged, none left, or reloading, $0836). Then the weapon's two-character name ($3363) and its colours at screen cells $E366/$E33E and $E36B/$E343 ($3367, $336B), each also written to the copy at $63xx
The first of the two characters naming each weapon (beam, then the three missile types), the second being the next character
The screen colours of each weapon's name, two tables of four ($3367 and $336B)
The second colour table of weapon_colours, written to $E36C/$E344

The TAC's data page. With no target, an empty name line, the hit points of the player ($345D) and the systems ($3480). For a ship target (slots 0-5): name ($33B5), its own target ($33EA), the range ($33F8), its tactic ($3435), hit points and systems. Any other target: name and range. Ends in $87FE
Prints the target's type name ($0B12/$0B13) at column $0E, row $2E, padded with spaces to column $15; a reversed mark first when the target is a ship targeting the player
Prints the name of the target's own target ($366D) at column $15

Prints "RAN " and the range to the target: the distance from the player ($7947) plus 2 in its high byte, divided ($B5E0); $75 or more in the top byte prints "30+ km", otherwise the number ($9EBF) and "m"
Prints "TAC " and the ship's tactic ($043F), its name from the list of eight-byte names at $0CAE
Prints "ARM  " and the slot's hit points ($051D, $9EBF)
Prints "SYS " and six system letters, c f a e b m, for the bits $20 $10 $08 $04 $02 $01: a space for a system the ship's type does not have ($0C45), reversed for one damaged ($0409)
One letter of tac_systems: bit A of the type's systems ($0C45) and of the slot's damage ($0409) decide blank, reversed or plain; Y holds the letter
"30+ km", then the TAC labels "RAN " ($34EC), "TAC " ($34F1), "ARM  " ($34F6) and "SYS " ($34FC)
The operand of LDA abs,Y in print_string ($9BAA): $9B9B writes the string's address here; at rest it holds "RAN "'s address

The TAC's picture page: the player's target (or the player's own ship with none) drawn in the TAC window in 3D. Clears the window (pattern 1, $B788, $8E17 at x $70, y 9, $4F by $2D), sets the drawing scale ($66CA with $0200), draws the model ($354C), then $B839, puts back the main view's flag $3A and scale ($66CA with 0) and ends in $87FE

Draws slot $A2's model in the TAC: the viewing distance is the type's $0A63 word plus $02CE (kept at $366A); the orientation is the slot's 27-byte block at $044B (or the identity at $0DA8 for objects past slot 6, and for the player's own ship), the position is that of the target relative to the player ($92CC, $923E, $95A0, $9160, $934B, $91B0) so it is seen as from the cockpit. Then jumps into the model's own code through the type's model pointer ($08F8/$08F9) with the type's $0999 and $0A63 words in $76/$77 and $5F/$60
Nine bytes whose address tac_draw_model passes to the model's code in $74/$75, with $0D40 in $78/$79
The viewing distance tac_draw_model works out, three bytes
tac_distance's middle byte
tac_distance's top byte
Prints the three-character label of ship slot A, kept at $0421+3*A (each ship has one, from fill_slot)

The computer ships' minds, every 16th call (counter $3808): for each ship in slots 5-1 whose AI state ($041B) is not 0: works out the distance to its target ($7947, kept in $D0-$D4); every third time round (counter $3809), for a ship whose $0403 is clear, a ship without a target looks for one ($3701), one with a target reconsiders its attitude ($3739) and tactic ($375F). Every time, a ship with a target sets its speed ($37A8), steers ($3CAB) and may fire ($38C1). Then $3A2D

A ship without a target takes the one in $0439 if it has been given one; otherwise looks for an enemy ($3811). Found: it becomes the target ($0445), and $C6. None: AI state 1, tactic 0 (cruise) at that tactic's speed ($0C9A), and one time in eight $3CDC
Unless its AI state is 2, the ship decides how it stands to its target ($3BE0): AI state $FE to fight, or $FF with tactic 7 (flee)

For a ship that is fighting ($041B = $FE): beyond $0861 in distance the tactic is 2 (pursue). Otherwise one in ten (a random number of $E6 or more) changes tactic: from cruise or pursue to the type's own tactic ($0C38), from any other to one of seven drawn from ai_tactic_choices

Sets the ship's speed ($0415) from its tactic: the tactic's speed ($0C9A), or, against a ship target, by the tactic's speed rule ($0CA4): negative takes the target's speed ($7C21), 1 the average of the two, 2 one from the distance ($37E7), 0 leaves the tactic's speed
Speed rule 2: 5 when the target is behind (negative $D4 or $D2/$D3 below $FF7D), otherwise the tactic's speed while far ($D0/$D1 over $0861) and $4B while close
Counts ship_ai's calls from 16 down to the next pass
Counts ship_ai's passes 2, 1, 0: target, attitude and tactic are reconsidered at 0
The seven tactics ai_tactic draws from: close, follow, swerve, stand, circle, elude, ram

Looks among ship slots 0-5 (not itself, in use, $0403 clear) for the one its faction most dislikes ($387E most negative, $FE before $FF); if none, takes the target of a ship of a faction it is allied to (attitude 2). Returns the slot in Y, negative for none

How faction A stands to faction X: from the player (X = 4) it is the player's standing with that faction ($072E+A), except that a type-$0C ship (in Y) is hostile ($FF) while the player has a bounty ($0726/$0727) and neutral otherwise; a negative faction gives 0. Between two computer factions it is faction_table entry A*4+X. $FE is hostile, $FF unfriendly, 0 neutral, 1 friendly, 2 allied
How each of the four factions stands to each other, row by faction: 1 FF FF FE / 0 1 1 FF / FF 2 2 FE / FE FE FE 2

A fighting ship ($041B negative, $0403 clear) within $08A4 of its target fires three times in ten (a random number below $4D). The flag $BD is set when the value $7947 left in $D2-$D4 has a positive top byte and a low word at or above $FFCB as a signed comparison. Then three times in ten a missile of its type's kind ($0C5F + 8; none with a damaged launcher, $0409 bit 0, or a type without missiles), a type 11 missile only with $BD set; otherwise the beam ($20EC), with $BD set or when its type's beam value ($0C52) has bit 7 set

Key G, surrender. Clears the view and shows the surrender text ($CF88). It counts only with exactly one ship fighting the player and the first time ($0832): then the rank count $072B gains $072A. A faction hostile to the player refuses ($CF81); one time in five any other ignores it ($CF7F). Pirates (faction 2) ask for the bounty ($0726/$0727) plus 50 credits ($CF87, Y/N $3BA1): paid, the bounty is cleared ($CF86) and every ship leaves; too little money, $CF85. Any other faction asks for the cargo ($CF84): yes with an empty hold gives $CF83, otherwise the hold is emptied ($CF82) and the ships leave. Refusing gives $CF80

Checked after ship_ai: a badly damaged merchant offers its cargo. Only once per encounter ($0832), when the player's target is a ship of faction 1 targeting the player, with under a quarter of its type's hit points ($0AA9 word / 4), no other ship targeting it or the player. The chance, $43 in 100, is halved when the player has under a quarter of its own hit points and again when that faction is hostile to the player. Then the view shows the offer ($CF8D and a random cargo name, $2EF7 with 0-19, and "?") with AGREE or REFUSE ($3BA1): refused, $CF8C; agreed, $CF8B, and with room in the hold ($CF89 if full) one or two units of that cargo ($CF8A, cargo_add), its escorts and the ship leave, the standing with faction 1 may drop (one time in four), and $079A counts it when $079B is set
Shows the two-item menu AGREE / REFUSE ($99DE with the list at $3BD3) centred on the message window, then prints character $11. Returns Z set for AGREE
The closing quote and line breaks after an offer, then the pointers to "AGREE" and "REFUSE" ($3BD3) and the words themselves

Whether ship X fights target Y: a score from 4 less than A, plus the ship's hit points in eighths of its type's maximum, plus half the difference of the two types' rank values ($0C79), plus one when the factions are hostile, plus two when the target already has a given target ($0439), minus two when the ship has one, minus one for faction 1, plus two for faction 2, and exactly 2 for faction 3. Returns it in A: negative means flee. A target past slot 5 always gives 1
Changes the player's standing with faction Y by A, between -2 and 2; a negative faction or faction 3 is left alone

Steers a computer ship once it has stopped rotating: by its tactic's steering mode ($0C86): negative none, 3 random rates ($3CDC), 2 turn to the target's heading (its forward vector, $045D+27*slot, or $0DBA past slot 6), 0 turn toward the target, 1 turn away from it
Gives ship X random turn, pitch and roll rates, each -31 to 32 ($3D61)
A random rate from -31 to 32

Turns ship X toward the direction at ($74): rotates it into the ship's frame ($9160 with the ship's orientation), finds its two angles ($983B into $6F-$73), adds the tactic's offset ($0C90, 90 degrees for circle and so on) to the first, and sets the turn rate ($0516) and the pitch rate ($0508) from the two angles less the type's turning limit ($0BE2), clamped ($B447, $B5C5, $B771)
Makes a ship's three-character label in $85-$87 ($3E1D each)
A random digit 0-9 or capital letter A-Z

The 3D view's draw list, from $A488 each frame: clears every slot's on-screen flag ($0621), tests every object in use against the view ($3EB8 with the type's radius from $0A63), keeping up to 14 in view; then draws them from the farthest to the nearest: each time the remaining entry with the greatest depth ($0D7E/$0D70) is drawn ($6400 with carry set, then $7033) and taken off the list
The operand of LDX #: build_draw_list writes the number of entries less one here, the index the search for the farthest entry starts from
build_draw_list's count of entries still to draw

Whether the object at ($58) relative to the viewer ($5A) is in the view: its distance along the view axis must be within its radius of the front ($94E7, $0D3E), and its sideways and vertical distances inside the view's slopes ($B398 with $0D6A-$0D6F and $0D68-$0D69). The three view coordinates go to $FF05-$FF0D + 9*entry. In view: depth to $0D7E/$0D70, the slot to $0D9A, on-screen flag $0621 set, and the size from $66AF to $0D8C; a far, small object (size under $0B) is drawn at once ($6400) and the carry comes back clear. Carry set when it is to be drawn later
The last 12 bytes of SR, zeros that nothing reads
